what the 1837 act gives: Groom. Birthplace *** COLLA *** - the old name of *** ROSARIO, COLONIA. *** Father *** RAMON ***, mother *** MARIA GONZALES. ***
why it matters: *** ROW 120'S WHOLE FINDING RESTS ON HIM: his children account for San Jose, Flores and Florida, with Salto and Montevideo besides - one family spreading across the interior in a single generation. *** And until today he existed here only inside other people's notes.

what the 1837 act gives: Named as the groom's father. Fathering children c.1800-1820.
why it matters: *** The head of the household, and the reason Colonia is not a gap but an ORIGIN. *** *** Deliberately NOT merged with the Ramon LERENA born 1892 in Argentina who is also in this register ***, nor with the tree's *** Ramon Llerena Cubas *** who is given as father of Gabino of Flores. *** Two, possibly three, different men, and no evidence joins them. ***

what the 1837 act gives: Named as the groom's mother, indexed merely as *** 'Maria Gonzales'. ***
why it matters: This archive's own notes give her the fuller *** Maria Josefa. *** Both forms are kept, because they have not been reconciled on an image.

what the 1837 act gives: The bride. Her parents named on the act: *** JOSE MONTANO and IGNACIA BARREDO. ***
why it matters: *** Her children appear in the Flores and Montevideo death registrations as 'LERENA MONTANA' *** - which is how this family was recognised at all.
